column1: # Which conformance-root artefacts each package's conformance tests require.
# `.github/ci/suite-plan.sh` reads this table and the root it is given, and
# partitions the package set:
#   served    every declared artefact is present in the root -- the package
#             runs WITH `CURATOR_CONFORMANCE_ROOT` exported;
#   deferred  at least one declared artefact is absent -- the package runs
#             with the variable UNSET, taking the `CURATOR_CONFORMANCE_ROOT is
#             not set` path its own tests already implement, and the exact
#             missing artefact is named in the gate report.
# The partition is DERIVED FROM THE ROOT, never from the lane. Against a root
# that publishes the whole surface this module reads, the deferred set is empty
# and the entire module runs with the root exported; that is what
# `CI_REQUIRE_FULL_ROOT=1` asserts in the candidate lane, so a candidate run can
# never report success while a package quietly ran without its vectors.
# A row is what makes a missing artefact LOUD. Two shapes are loud, and they are
# the only two allowed:
#   * the package is listed here. A root missing a declared artefact defers the
#     whole package, the artefact is named in the plan, and the deferral is
#     fatal under CI_REQUIRE_FULL_ROOT=1. The package's cases then guard on the
#     UNSET ROOT only -- `t.Skip("CURATOR_CONFORMANCE_ROOT is not set")`, class
#     `root-unset`, which `skip-classes.tsv` admits only for a deferred package.
#   * the package is absent from this table and reads its artefacts with no
#     guard at all, so a missing file goes RED with the open() error naming it.
# A THIRD shape is not allowed and is what this table exists to keep out: a
# per-artefact `t.Skipf("%s publishes no ... vector", root)` in a package that
# is absent from this table. That skip classifies as `root-content`, which is
# policy `allow` in EVERY lane, so the candidate lane stays green while the
# cases it was asked to run quietly do not run. `internal/interop` carried six
# such guards over four environments vector families and declared none of them;
# the fix was to split those cases into `internal/interop/environments` and list it
# here, so the pre-environments cases in `internal/interop` keep running on the
# committed pin while a candidate that drops a family fails by name.
# Columns are TAB separated:
#   package  artefact[,artefact...]  note
# package
